title: Default 600s delegate timeout too short for L/XL tickets
source_context: Sprint in rick-terminal, 2026-07-03; resumes with stored session_id worked well as workaround
description: An L-complexity ticket (CodeMirror editor pane, RICK-028 in rick-terminal) hit the 600s timeout twice in a row; each run made progress but was killed mid-flight. The delegate already prints 'Consider splitting the ticket' but Rick has to manually resume with --timeout. Better: scale the default timeout with ticket complexity (S=600, M=900, L=1800, XL=2700) or auto-resume once with a doubled timeout before failing.
proposed_changes: In delegate.py, read ticket complexity and multiply the default timeout; keep --timeout as explicit override.

triage.evidence: scripts/delegate.py:3338 `p.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=600, help="Timeout in seconds (default: 600)")`; no complexity-based timeout logic exists (complexity only feeds _COMPLEXITY_BUDGET_MAP/_COMPLEXITY_EFFORT_MAP at lines 1276-1293). Timeout handler (~2977) only saves session_id and prints a manual `--resume` hint — no auto-retry. orchestrate.py run_delegate (line 227-233) still hardcodes timeout=600 and passes `--timeout 600` explicitly at 8+ call sites. sleepy.py:58 DEFAULT_DELEGATE_TIMEOUT=1800 shows only the overnight path was patched.
triage.note: Still valid: delegate.py default timeout is a flat 600s with no complexity scaling and no auto-resume on timeout. Only sleepy.py got a 1800s workaround (commit b680ed9 era); the interactive delegate path and all orchestrate.py call sites still use 600s. Note: orchestrate.py explicitly passes --timeout 600 to the delegate subprocess, so a complete fix should also update those call sites (or have them omit --timeout), slightly widening scope beyond the declared target_files. Core change remains a focused delegate.py edit: map ticket estimated_complexity (S/M/L/XL) to a default timeout, keep explicit --timeout as override (switch argparse default to None to detect explicit use).
